A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GTR research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained material can be matched despite figure relocation, renumbering, and appendix expansion.

before.justification: v1 reports original GTR experiments on Points24, other gym_cards tasks, and ALFWorld, including training curves, ablations, and example trajectories.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds Qwen2.5-VL training results, corrector comparisons, textual-observation controls, and extended-training outcomes.

M1.justification: The substantive procedure retains PPO plus supervised thought cloning, automated correction, DAgger, tool use, format controls, and episode truncation. Mathematical corrections and tests with alternative backbones or correctors do not establish a changed implemented algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds GTR evaluation with textual ALFWorld observations, whereas v1 evaluates GTR using images and action history. Text-enabled comparator results already appeared in v1. Points24, Numberline, EZPoints, Blackjack, and the six ALFWorld task categories remain covered.

E2.justification: Figure 6 adds OpenAI o3 as a reported reference comparator. Comparator membership in Tables 1–3 is retained. The introduction's corrected Qwen2-VL name matches the existing table baseline rather than establishing a baseline replacement.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands the tested configurations through Qwen2.5-VL-7B agent training, Qwen2.5-VL-72B and 7B correctors, controlled ALFWorld text-input comparisons, and an additional 30,000-step GTR experiment. The original Table 4 settings remain unchanged; the longer GTR experiment supplements the default training budget.

E4.justification: New analyses examine corrector choice and computational overhead (Table 5), dependence on textual observations (Table 6), and stability beyond the usual training horizon (Figure 13). Appendix F adds successful GTR trajectories and replaces the ALFWorld failure example with a paired comparison. Existing component ablations are retained.

E5.justification: v2 adds shaded bands to the retained ALFWorld and ablation curves in Figures 7–9; their v1 counterparts showed lines alone. Figure 5 already had bands. Neither version defines their statistical meaning or supplies run counts, so additional replications cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include the Qwen agent comparison, where GTR's best curve reaches the o3 reference while its central curve remains lower; corrector-dependent GTR success of 17.5% versus 6.5% for GPT-4o versus Qwen2.5-VL-72B; and GTR ALFWorld success of 21.0% with text versus 17.8% without. Extended-training and trajectory outcomes are also added. Table 3's GTR aggregate changes from 0.17 to 0.18 while its subtask entries remain unchanged; Tables 1–2 retain their values.

T1.justification: Equation 2 adds conditioning on thought tokens when calculating action-token probabilities, a mathematical correction beyond notation changes. Equation 4 also changes the clipped PPO ratio to observation probabilities given states, inconsistent with its action-based unclipped term. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central thought-collapse diagnosis, automated process-guidance contribution, and claims of improved performance from smaller models. The new experiments extend supporting evidence without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B.3 newly discusses corrector overhead and attributes Qwen2.5-VL-72B's poorer performance to tool-use limitations and the 7B corrector's failure to formatting problems. Appendix C interprets the text-observation comparison as evidence that correction bridges visual and textual information. Earlier mechanism explanations largely remain intact.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link and reports corrector-specific token usage, estimated costs, and training times in Table 5. Existing hyperparameters, hardware information, and corrector prompts are retained. The relationship between Table 5's GPT-4o time of 86 hours and the retained approximately 30-hour training statement is not explained.

R1.justification: Section 4.2 newly credits the already-cited embodied multimodal agent work [56], alongside Thought Cloning [15], as inspiration for incorporating supervised guidance. The cited-work set and broader research positioning remain unchanged; the MUEP reference update is bibliographic.

P1.justification: v2 makes distributed copyedits, standardizes model names, updates author information, and subdivides the training appendix. Prompts move from Appendix C to E, and trajectory examples move from D to F. The main section sequence and most prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The visual presentation expands through new result Figures 6 and 13 and Tables 5–6, redrawn ALFWorld and ablation plots with shaded bands and revised axes, and two task-specific baseline/GTR trajectory displays replacing one combined collapse display. Several retained figures and tables are also resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 strengthens validation through a newer backbone, longer training, and textual-observation controls, while making corrector costs and failures more transparent. These are useful gains, tempered by undefined shaded bands, sparse o3 comparison details, unreconciled timing statements, and the new inconsistency in Equation 4.
